concepts.title: Number Theory
concepts.definition: The field that studies how whole numbers build sequences, and which regularities those sequences show, is commonly called the theory of numbers.
concepts.key_idea: Looking for order among 0, 1, 2, 3, ... and explaining why counting sequences behave so regularly.
question_patterns: What is number theory?
Define the branch of mathematics that studies whole number patterns
Which branch of math deals with number sequences?
Describe the questions that number theory tries to answer
Which area of mathematics looks at counting sequences and their regularities?

solution_steps.action: identify the subject
solution_steps.explain: The study of patterns in whole numbers is defined as number theory.

solution_steps.action: list the whole number sequence and observe regularities
solution_steps.explain: Whole numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, ... follow a fixed counting order, which is the starting point for number theory.

solution_steps.action: confirm the definition applies to the question
solution_steps.explain: Any question about how counting sequences behave or why they show regularity falls under number theory.

concepts.title: Triangular Numbers
concepts.definition: Counts of dots that stack into a triangle: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, ... Each fresh row holds one more dot than the row above it.
concepts.key_idea: T(n) = 1 + 2 + ... + n = n x (n + 1) / 2 -- each added row grows the picture by one more dot.
question_patterns: Find the nth triangular number
What is the value of the triangular number at position n?
Calculate the nth term of the sequence 1, 3, 6, 10...
How many dots are in the nth triangular pattern?
How much is the 10th triangular number?
What is T(7) in the sequence 1, 3, 6, 10, 15...?

solution_steps.action: find next integer
solution_steps.explain: The formula involves n and n+1

solution_steps.action: multiply and divide
solution_steps.explain: The nth triangular number is half the product of n and n+1

solution_steps.action: verify the result matches the dot-stacking pattern
solution_steps.explain: Each new row adds one more dot than the previous row, so the total dots form a triangle of height n.

concepts.title: Square Numbers
concepts.definition: Counts of dots that fill a square grid: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ... You get them by taking a number times itself.
concepts.key_idea: n x n dots tile an n by n grid; the running totals of odd values (1, 1+3, 1+3+5, ...) build exactly these counts.
question_patterns: How many dots fill the nth square-dot grid: 1, 4, 9, 16...?
Find the nth square number
What is the square of n?
Calculate the nth term in the sequence 1, 4, 9, 16...
How many dots form a square of side n?
How much is the 12th square number?
What value does 9 x 9 give in the sequence 1, 4, 9, 16...?

solution_steps.action: multiply n by itself
solution_steps.explain: The area of a square grid with side n is n squared

solution_steps.action: confirm the result fills an n by n grid
solution_steps.explain: An n by n grid holds exactly n*n dots, matching the sequence 1, 4, 9, 16, ...

solution_steps.action: check against the odd-number running total
solution_steps.explain: The sum of the first n odd numbers also equals n*n, providing a second way to verify the square count.

concepts.title: Cube Numbers
concepts.definition: Counts of dots that pack a cube: 1, 8, 27, 64, ... You get them by taking a number times itself, twice over.
concepts.key_idea: Cubing, n ** 3, counts an n by n by n block of unit cubes.
question_patterns: Find the nth cube number
What is n cubed?
Calculate the nth term in the sequence 1, 8, 27, 64...
How many dots are in a cube of side n?
How much is the 5th cube number?
What do you get when 6 is cubed?

solution_steps.action: raise n to the power of 3
solution_steps.explain: The volume of a cube with side n is n cubed

solution_steps.action: confirm the result fills an n by n by n block
solution_steps.explain: An n by n by n arrangement of unit cubes holds exactly n**3 dots, matching the sequence 1, 8, 27, 64, ...

solution_steps.action: verify against the hexagonal-number running total
solution_steps.explain: The sum of the first n hexagonal numbers equals n**3, giving a second check on the cube count.

concepts.title: Sum of Consecutive Odd Numbers
concepts.definition: Add up odd values beginning at 1 -- 1 + 3 + 5 + ... -- and the running answer keeps landing on a square count.
concepts.key_idea: After the opening k odd values the total is k x k; every fresh odd value grows the picture into the next square.
question_patterns: Find the sum of the first n odd numbers
What is the sum of 1 + 3 + 5 + ... up to n terms?
Calculate the sum of the first 100 odd numbers
How much is the sum of odd numbers from 1 to 2n-1?
Calculate the total of the opening 50 odd values.
What is 1 plus 3 plus 5 plus 7 plus 9?

solution_steps.action: square the count of numbers
solution_steps.explain: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared

solution_steps.action: identify the nth odd number as 2n-1
solution_steps.explain: The odd numbers being added are 1, 3, 5, ..., (2n-1), confirming there are n terms in the sum.

solution_steps.action: verify the total matches a square-dot count
solution_steps.explain: Each added odd value grows the dot picture into the next square, so the running total after n terms is n*n.

concepts.title: Sum of Counting Numbers Up and Down
concepts.definition: Climb 1 + 2 + ... up to some peak, then descend back to 1; the grand total always equals the peak times itself.
question_patterns: Find the sum of numbers 1 to n and back to 1
What is the value of 1 + 2 + ... + peak + ... + 2 + 1?
Calculate the sum up and down with peak n
Find the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 1
Calculate the up-and-down total whose peak is 10.

solution_steps.action: square the peak value
solution_steps.explain: The sum of the sequence increasing to n and decreasing to 1 is n squared

solution_steps.action: count the terms on each side of the peak
solution_steps.explain: The sequence has (peak-1) terms rising to the peak and (peak-1) terms falling back, plus the peak itself.

solution_steps.action: verify the total matches a square-dot grid
solution_steps.explain: Two interlocking staircases of dots form a peak by peak square, confirming the sum equals peak*peak.

concepts.title: Sum of Consecutive Triangular Numbers
concepts.definition: Take any triangular count, add the very next one, and the answer is always a square count.
concepts.key_idea: T(n-1) + T(n) = n x n -- two staircases interlock into an n by n grid.
question_patterns: What is the sum of the (n-1)th and nth triangular numbers?
Add consecutive triangular numbers at positions n-1 and n
Show that the sum of two consecutive triangular numbers is a square
Find the total when T(6) and T(7) are added.
Which square count equals T(8) + T(9)?

solution_steps.action: square the larger index
compute each triangular number separately
solution_steps.explain: T(n-1) = (n-1)*n/2 and T(n) = n*(n+1)/2, so their sum can be checked term by term.

solution_steps.action: verify the two triangles interlock into a square
solution_steps.explain: Two staircases of dots fit together to fill an n by n grid, confirming the sum is n*n.

concepts.title: Hexagonal Numbers
concepts.definition: A growing sequence 1, 7, 19, 37, ... whose dot picture wraps one ring around a hexagon at every stage.
concepts.key_idea: H(n) = 1 + 6 x T(n-1), i.e. 3n(n-1) + 1 -- each ring holds six more dots than the previous ring.
question_patterns: Find the nth hexagonal number
Calculate the nth term of 1, 7, 19, 37...
What is the next number in the hexagonal sequence?
How much is the 6th hexagonal number?
Calculate the hexagon count at position 10.

solution_steps.action: find product of n and n-1
solution_steps.explain: The formula uses n and the previous integer

solution_steps.action: multiply by 3 and add 1
solution_steps.explain: The nth hexagonal term is 3*n*(n-1) + 1

solution_steps.action: verify the result matches the hexagon ring picture
solution_steps.explain: Each new ring around the hexagon adds six more dots than the previous ring, so the total follows 1 + 6*T(n-1).

concepts.title: Sum of Hexagonal Numbers
concepts.definition: Total up 1 + 7 + 19 + 37 + ... (the hexagon counts) and the answer lands on a cube count every time.
concepts.key_idea: Totalling the opening n hexagon counts yields n ** 3.
question_patterns: Find the sum of the first n hexagonal numbers
What do you get when you add 1 + 7 + 19 + ... up to n terms?
Calculate the sum of hexagonal numbers up to position n
How much is 1 + 7 + 19 + 37 + 61?
Calculate the total of the opening 4 hexagon counts.

solution_steps.action: cube the count
solution_steps.explain: The sum of the first n hexagonal numbers is n cubed

solution_steps.action: list the hexagonal terms being added
solution_steps.explain: The terms are 1, 7, 19, 37, ... and each is found using 3*k*(k-1)+1 for k from 1 to n.

solution_steps.action: verify the running total lands on a cube
solution_steps.explain: Adding the hexagon counts one by one gives totals 1, 8, 27, 64, ..., which are exactly the cube numbers.

concepts.title: Regular Polygons Properties
concepts.definition: A closed, straight-sided figure in which every side matches every other in measure and every corner matches every other in size.
concepts.key_idea: Each side of a regular polygon closes at exactly one corner, so the two counts always agree.
question_patterns: How many corners does a regular polygon with n sides have?
Compare the number of sides and corners in a regular pentagon
If a regular polygon has n corners, how many sides does it have?
How many sides does a regular polygon with 7 corners have?
What holds true for side lengths and angles in a regular hexagon?

solution_steps.action: equate sides and corners
solution_steps.explain: In any closed polygon, the number of sides equals the number of corners.

solution_steps.action: check that all sides have equal length
solution_steps.explain: A regular polygon requires every side to match every other side in measure.

solution_steps.action: check that all angles have equal size
solution_steps.explain: A regular polygon also requires every corner angle to match every other corner angle, confirming full regularity.

concepts.title: Koch Snowflake Segments
concepts.definition: A fractal curve built by swapping every straight piece for a small hump motif, then repeating that swap at ever smaller scales.
concepts.key_idea: Each round multiplies the piece count by 4, so after n-1 rounds a triangle edge set holds 3 x 4**(n-1) pieces.
question_patterns: How many line segments are in the nth iteration of the Koch snowflake?
Calculate the number of segments in Koch snowflake at step n
Find the total line segments if the sequence starts 3, 12, 48...
How many pieces does the Koch curve hold at iteration 4?
Calculate the piece count after 3 rounds of hump replacement.

solution_steps.action: determine power of 4
solution_steps.explain: The number of segments grows by a factor of 4 each step, starting from 3 segments at n=1

solution_steps.action: calculate total segments
solution_steps.explain: Multiply 3 by 4 raised to the power of (n-1)

solution_steps.action: verify the growth factor of 4
solution_steps.explain: Each iteration replaces every straight segment with 4 smaller segments, so the count multiplies by 4 each step.
